title: Undergraduate Aerodynamics
subtitle: Vortex-dominated flows and the physics of lift — from potential-flow foundations through thin-airfoil and lifting-line theory to the aerodynamics of the whole aircraft.
startNote: Classes begin Monday, 27 July 2026. Lecture materials will be posted here through the term.
assessmentLead: Continuous by design — the term is graded through weekly tutorial quizzes, two quizzes, and a comprehensive end-semester exam.

assessment.d: Short quiz at every tutorial + assignments
15 min on a real-world aerodynamics topic

rules: A short, closed-book quiz at each tutorial — lectures, an assigned reading, or both.
The first tutorial quiz is ungraded — a no-stakes run to learn the format.
Your lowest three graded quizzes are dropped — also your absence allowance (miss up to three tutorials, no make-up).
Assignments carry a 10% penalty per late day, up to 3 days.
One make-up exam only, after the end-sem, for any one missed quiz/exam.
No separate professionalism grade this semester.

windows.title: Window 1
rows: Introduction to aerodynamics; lift/drag/moment; applications & history; course & tutorial policies
Review — vector calculus: grad/div/curl; divergence & Stokes' theorems
Review — fluid kinematics: continuum, material derivative, Eulerian/Lagrangian, streamlines
Conservation laws (continuity, momentum); incompressibility; irrotationality; velocity potential
Stream function; Laplace equation; boundary conditions; superposition
Elementary flows I — uniform flow, source/sink, doublet
Elementary flows II — Rankine half-body; non-lifting flow over a cylinder
Lifting flow over a cylinder; Kutta–Joukowski theorem  L = ρV∞Γ
Vortex dynamics — Helmholtz's theorems; Kelvin's circulation theorem
Biot–Savart law; vortex filament; vortex sheet
Airfoil nomenclature & characteristics; cₗ, c_d, c_m; pressure distribution; aerodynamic centre
Kutta condition; starting vortex; generation of circulation on an airfoil

windows.title: Window 2
rows: Thin-airfoil theory I — vortex sheet on the camber line; fundamental equation
Thin-airfoil theory II — symmetric airfoil: cₗ = 2πα; a.c. at c/4
Thin-airfoil theory III — cambered airfoil: Fourier-series solution; cₗ, c_m
Thin-airfoil theory IV — moments; centre of pressure vs. aerodynamic centre
Method of singularities; source/vortex panel methods — concept & discretisation
Vortex panel method — implementation; intro to computational aerodynamics
Experimental airfoil characteristics — Reynolds effects, stall, drag polar
Propellers I — momentum (actuator-disc) theory; thrust; ideal efficiency
Propellers II — blade-element theory (uses 2D airfoil data)
Propellers III — combined blade-element–momentum (BEM); performance charts

windows.title: Window 3
rows: Finite wings — downwash; induced angle of attack; induced drag; wingtip vortices
Prandtl's lifting-line theory I — the fundamental equation
Lifting-line theory II — elliptical lift distribution; minimum induced drag; span efficiency
Lifting-line theory III — general distribution (Fourier); aspect-ratio effects
Effect of geometry — aspect ratio, taper, twist on lift & induced drag
Elements of lifting-surface theory; vortex-lattice concept
Swept & delta wings — sweep effects; leading-edge vortices
Flow past bodies in incompressible flow; drag breakdown (pressure vs. friction)
Lift, drag & moment of the whole airplane; aircraft drag polar; L/D
Putting it together: airfoil → wing → aircraft; applications
Course synthesis & outlook (compressibility preview); End-sem review I
End-sem review II — worked problems & Q&A (Last Instructional Day)
END-SEMESTER EXAM — covers the entire course

references.text: Anderson, J. D. — Fundamentals of Aerodynamics, 7th ed.
Kuethe, A. M. & Chow, C.-Y. — Foundations of Aerodynamics, 5th ed.
Kundu, Cohen, Dowling & Capecelatro — Fluid Mechanics, 6th ed.
